identity.title: MoDeGPT: Modular Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression

problem.claim: Compress LLMs for deployment on resource-limited devices while preserving performance and reducing computational demands.

gap.claim: Existing low-rank compression methods are reported to incur substantial accuracy loss or added parameter and inference-time overhead.

contributions.claim: MoDeGPT jointly decomposes consecutive Transformer subcomponents, reduces hidden dimensions through larger-scale output reconstruction, and repurposes Nyström approximation, CR decomposition, and SVD.
The proposed decomposition approach is designed to provide bounded errors.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present Modular De-composition (MoDeGPT) as a new, efficient, structured compression framework intended to overcome limitations of prior methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MoDeGPT, without backward propagation, consistently matches or surpasses prior gradient-dependent techniques and reduces compute costs by 98% when compressing a 13B-parameter model.
On LLaMA-2/3 and OPT models, the authors report retaining 90–95% of zero-shot performance at compression rates of 25–30%.
The authors report that compression can finish on a single GPU within a few hours and increase inference throughput by up to 46%.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM resource demands limit deployment on constrained devices, while low-rank methods may trade away accuracy or add overhead.
The paper introduces MoDeGPT as a structured compression framework.
It jointly decomposes consecutive Transformer subcomponents, reconstructs outputs at larger structural scale, and uses three classical matrix decompositions with intended bounded errors.
Experiments report competitive or better performance without backpropagation, substantial compute reduction, retained zero-shot performance, and higher throughput.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific structural design—joint decomposition and output reconstruction—to both an error-control objective and deployment metrics.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a method-to-evidence chain easier to assess by connecting design choices to measurable resource and quality outcomes.
lessons.application: When presenting a compression method, explicitly pair each structural mechanism with its intended constraint and report quality, cost, and throughput under named model settings.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no concrete mechanism-to-metric relationship or when the abstract cannot support the relevant conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baseline identities, statistical variability, evaluation-set details, or the precise definitions of compression rate and compute cost.
The magnitude and formal conditions of the claimed bounded-error guarantee are not given.
The reported ranges and throughput maximum are not tied to individual models or configurations.
